limitations: One exact native SMS or MMS bridge call and its pending owner, one worker journal lookup, one main-queue native dialog, one owner Send tap, one queued dispatch, and one cancellation or foreground retirement. At most one platform invocation and one result; fixed operation and binding identity.

The call owner exists before the journal work is queued and remains until the original call resolves or rejects. Cancellation marks matching outstanding owners before its own acknowledgement. A retired owner cannot open a later dialog or dispatch after a Send tap waits on the worker. A recorded or admitted result is retained through cancellation. An unrelated operation cannot retire this owner.

The mandatory Android Gradle check compiles the real TelephonyPlugin and SmsTelephony and executes actual bridge methods under Robolectric29 with controlled worker/Main queues, a granted test foreground/SIM and an in-memory native journal. Six new cases exercise initial SMS/MMS cancellation, lifecycle retirement, cancellation after Send, unrelated cancellation, and already recorded submission readback. The existing SMS/MMS journal suites also execute; exact testcase names and zero skips are required.

The state model is a finite native queue boundary projection, not a refinement proof. The single abstract invocation does not enumerate multipart or multi-recipient partial sends. Native journal suites supplement those cases. Simultaneous independent hosts, arbitrary Android lifecycle delivery, storage write failures, callback batching/listener fanout, carrier/provider acceptance, real SIM roles/permissions and physical Android foreground-service behavior are outside this projection. Robolectric ports prove no radio or carrier delivery.
